findings.title: Frontmatter read failures are misclassified as `doctype` validation failures
findings.description: At `packages/core/src/schema/sliceDesignFiles.ts:95`, `validateFile()` relies on `parseFrontmatter(file)` before it performs its own wrapped `readFile()` at lines 101-105. `parseFrontmatter()` reads at `packages/core/src/introspection/parsers/frontmatterParser.ts:17-18` and has a blanket `catch` at lines 68-69 that returns `{ found: false, data: {} }` on any error. Therefore an I/O failure in that first read — for example a file becoming unreadable after `preflight()`'s `stat`/`access` checks at `packages/core/src/schema/sliceDesignFiles.ts:73-86` — becomes `frontmatter.data.docType !== 'slice-design'` and returns a normal `reason: doctype` failure at lines 96-97. The CLI then sets exit code 1 at `packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:83-85` instead of routing a thrown `SliceDesignValidationError` through `handleError(err, 2)` at lines 100-103. Read the document once in the file layer and parse frontmatter from that text, or make the parser error-aware, so read failures are wrapped consistently and exit 2.

findings.title: Public validation result type permits illegal states
findings.description: `DesignValidationResult` at `packages/core/src/schema/sliceDesignFiles.ts:42-49` uses `pass: boolean`, `missing: string[]`, and an optional `reason`, so it allows states such as `{ pass: true, reason: 'doctype' }` and `{ pass: false, missing: ['## Value'], reason: 'doctype' }`. The CLI compensates with runtime checks at `packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:50-57` (`result.pass ? ...` and `result.reason === DesignFailureReason.DocType`). This shape is exported as a public core API at `packages/core/src/node.ts:30-37` and serialized as the command’s JSON contract at `packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:25-31`. The TypeScript rules require illegal states to be unrepresentable and prefer discriminated unions over runtime string checks. Use `pass` as a discriminant or introduce a `kind`/`status` union while preserving the documented JSON fields.

findings.title: New TypeScript source files do not follow the required kebab-case file naming convention
findings.description: The TypeScript project rules require source files to be kebab-case. The newly added modules are camelCase: `packages/cli/src/commands/validateDesign.ts:1`, `packages/core/src/schema/sliceDesignFiles.ts:1`, and `packages/core/src/schema/sliceDesignValidator.ts:1`. The new CLI test already uses kebab-case at `packages/cli/tests/commands/validate-design.test.ts:1`, which makes the source naming drift more visible. Rename the new source files to `validate-design.ts`, `slice-design-files.ts`, and `slice-design-validator.ts`, then update imports and exports accordingly.
